name: Lifetime Value Over a Fixed Horizon
description: Value a customer over a defined contract or planning window rather than their full expected lifetime.
formula: Months retained = min(1 / Churn Rate, Horizon); LTV = ARPU x Gross Margin x Months Retained
business_contexts: a B2B software vendor valuing customers over a three-year contract
a telecom operator assessing value within a fixed handset contract
a private equity buyer valuing a subscription base over its hold period
an insurance provider modelling policyholder value across a renewal window
a gym chain valuing members over an annual membership term
question_patterns: What is the value of a customer over the stated horizon?
How much gross profit does a customer generate within the analysis window?
What is the lifetime value of a customer across the contract period?
Over the planning horizon, what is each customer worth?
solution_logic: Step 1: Monthly gross profit per customer = arpu_monthly x gross_margin_pct
Step 2: Average customer lifetime in months = 1 / monthly_churn_rate
Step 3: Months retained = the smaller of average lifetime and horizon_months
Step 4: Lifetime value over horizon = monthly gross profit x months retained
key_insight: A customer cannot be worth more than the window you are valuing them over. When the horizon is shorter than the average lifetime, the horizon caps the value.
common_mistakes: Applying the infinite-horizon formula when the question specifies a fixed window
Failing to compare average lifetime against the horizon before multiplying
Using revenue rather than gross profit per month
framework_soundbite: Value the customer over the window you actually have. Take the shorter of average lifetime and the horizon.
